candidates.title: Integration accuracy and order
candidates.computes: The same Newtonian point-mass system from the file's `initial` block, integrated for one period of its tightest pair T_s (the pair of least initial separation as a circular orbit, as integrators-compared defines it) with four fixed-step schemes (explicit Euler, symplectic Euler, velocity Verlet, RK4) at n = 50, 100, 200, 400, 800 steps per T_s; the error at the end is the largest body displacement from the reference (scipy solve_ivp DOP853, rtol = atol = 1e-13, same equations); the observed order is the least-squares slope of ln(error) against ln(h) over the five steps.
candidates.oracle: tools/compute-gate-oracle.py, own integrator code written separately, with the same DOP853 reference call

legs.what: errors against the oracle's: every (scheme, n) relative 1e-6; the four orders absolute 1e-4
legs.bound: 1e-6 / 1e-4 (the two codes integrate the same equations with the same arithmetic and the same reference, so they agree to rounding)

legs.what: observed order against theory (1, 1, 2, 4): |p - p_theory| <= 0.1 p_theory + 0.1
legs.bound: 0.2, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5 (a log-log fit over a factor 16 in h; 10 percent of the order plus a pre-asymptotic allowance of 0.1, fixed here before any fit)

legs.what: determinism: two fresh `python3 -I` runs give the same answer text
negative case: the same file with the second body's initial position set equal to the first's (a collision at t = 0) is refused
legs.bound: the run raises and returns no answer

legs.what: supplies: imports within {numpy, scipy, matplotlib, astropy, the standard library}; no file, network, subprocess or eval of input text; the example input validates as a `gravitas.orbital-system/1` through js/systemSpec.js systemFromFile and is unchanged (sha256)

candidates.title: Adaptive steps
candidates.computes: The same system and span as N01 integrated with an embedded Dormand-Prince 5(4) pair written in the notebook, error per step scaled by atol + rtol|y| with atol = rtol = tol, rms norm, safety 0.9, step factor limited to [0.2, 5], tol = 1e-4, 1e-6, 1e-8, 1e-10; it reports accepted and rejected steps, function evaluations, the final error against the same DOP853 reference as N01 (divided by the widest distance from the barycenter, r_far), and the function evaluations the fixed-step RK4 of N01 needs (n doubled from 50, at most 102,400) to reach the same final error.
candidates.oracle: scipy.integrate.solve_ivp method RK45 (the same coefficient set, a different controller) at rtol = atol = tol

legs.what: global error control: final error / r_far <= 100 tol at every tol
legs.bound: 100 tol (global error accumulates over many steps; two orders is the customary allowance for a local control, fixed before the run)

legs.what: against scipy RK45 at the same tol: the ratio of final errors in [0.2, 5] and the ratio of accepted steps in [0.5, 2]
legs.bound: both ratios (same scheme, different step-factor constants)

legs.what: determinism

negative case: the file with the second body placed 1e-6 of the first pair separation from the first is refused (more than 200,000 accepted plus rejected steps, or a step below 1e-12 of the span) rather than looping
legs.bound: raises, and does so in at most 20 s of CPython CPU time

legs.what: supplies, as N01.e
reported, not a verdict: the fixed-step RK4's function evaluations divided by the adaptive scheme's at tol 1e-8

candidates.title: Orbital chaos from exported engine runs

input.example: made by the spike from the engine: tools/compute-gate-pair-runs.mjs runs family D's initial conditions (tests/fixtures/dynamics/initial-conditions.json, seed 101) twice in js/physics.js as tools/dynamics-runs.mjs runs them, the second with the x coordinate of body 0 increased by 1e-6 (Heggie length), 150 snapshots at 0.1 crossing time; one axis `snapshot` (0 to 150), the output `separation` = the Euclidean distance in the full phase space (positions, velocities, 4N numbers) between the two runs; a gravitas.grid/1 that validateGrid accepts

candidates.computes: The exponential growth rate of the separation: S = the median of the last 20 snapshots; the window runs from the first snapshot at which separation > 3 x separation[0] to the last snapshot before separation > 0.1 S; lambda = the ordinary least-squares slope of ln(separation) against time (in crossing times, 0.1 per snapshot) over the window; also R^2 of that fit, the window's length and the Lyapunov time 1/lambda. A window of fewer than 10 snapshots, or R^2 < 0.98, is 'not constrained' and refused.
candidates.oracle: tools/compute-gate-oracle.py: the same window rule and numpy.polyfit, written separately; plus three synthetic grids with a known answer

legs.what: analytic cases: a logistic-saturating exponential separation s(t) = S s0 e^(lambda t) / (S + s0 e^(lambda t)), S = 1, s0 = 1e-6, t = 0.1 k, k = 0 to 150, for lambda = 0.7 and 1.5 per crossing time: lambda recovered within 5 percent
legs.bound: 5 percent (the logistic factor bends the log slope by at most 9 percent at the window's end; 5 percent is the allowance on the window average, fixed here)

legs.what: against the oracle on the engine's pair: lambda, the window's two ends and R^2 agree
legs.bound: lambda and R^2 absolute 1e-9, window ends equal

legs.what: determinism

negative cases (both must be refused): (i) linear growth s(t) = s0 (1 + 100 t); (ii) a pair whose separation starts at order 1 (two different clusters, seeds 101 and 102 of family D: the notebook's input is then not a pair of neighbouring runs)
supplies, as N01.e; the example input validates through js/dataKinds/contract.js validateGrid
reported: lambda and the Lyapunov time of the engine's pair, in crossing times, and the saturation S

candidates.title: Root finding for Kepler's equation

input.example: compute/inputs/kepler-16.gravitas-system.json (existing; the companions' `e` values enter the list)

candidates.computes: E - e sin E = M for the mesh M = 2 pi k / 720 (k = 0 to 720) and also M = 1e-6, 1e-3 and 2 pi - 1e-3, for e in the file's companion eccentricities and {0.5, 0.9, 0.99, 0.999}, by Newton's method, by bisection and by Halley's method, each from the starting value E0 = M; it reports the iterations to |dE| <= 1e-14 (cap 100 for Newton and Halley, 100 for bisection) and the number of failures to converge per method and e, and the observed Newton order at e = 0.5: p = median over the mesh of ln(err_{k+2}/err_{k+1}) / ln(err_{k+1}/err_k) at the first k with err_k < 1e-2 and err_{k+2} > 1e-14.
candidates.oracle: scipy.optimize.brentq on [M - e, M + e] with xtol = 1e-15, rtol = 8.9e-16 (independent bracketing method)

legs.what: against the oracle: every converged root of the notebook's bisection (the method that cannot fail inside the bracket) within 1e-11 rad
against js/orbital.js solveKepler (Gravitas's own solver, pinned output over the same mesh): every root within 1e-11 rad of the notebook's bisection root
determinism
negative cases: an input whose companion has e = 1.2 and one with e = -0.1 are refused (the equation's domain is 0 <= e < 1)
supplies, as N01.e
observed Newton order at e = 0.5
reported, not a verdict: which methods fail to converge from E0 = M at e = 0.99 and 0.999 (the teaching point of the notebook)

candidates.title: Least squares from scratch against Prompt 154

input.example: compute/inputs/tess-hd209458-s56.observation.json (existing): the first 600 cadences, columns time, flux, flux-error

against Prompt 154's js/kernels/statistics fTest, called with the notebook's own chi^2 as the sums of squares and its n and parameter counts: F relative 1e-9; p relative 1e-8 where p > 1e-300
determinism
negative cases (both refused): a window with fewer points than degree 4 needs (five points are required; the test gives four), and a window whose times are all equal (a rank-deficient design)

candidates.title: A periodogram from scratch against the existing family
candidates.computes: The Lomb-Scargle power with a floating mean (unweighted, the fraction of the variance one sinusoid and a mean explain) at 400 periods log-spaced from 0.5 to 10 d, written in numpy from the least-squares definition (a 3-by-3 normal system per period), not from astropy; the peak period; the power at the peak.

candidates.title: Interpolation of isochrone tables

input.example: made by the spike: tools/compute-gate-iso-input.mjs writes the MIST pack's six columns (feh, logAge, phase, mass, g, r; js/data/observations/mistSdssIsochrones.js decoded through js/tableObservation.js) as one observation document of kind `table`, unchanged values

candidates.computes: At the table's [Fe/H] nearest zero (ties to the lower), phase 0 (main sequence): for each interior age a_k (k = 1 to K-2) the held-out absolute r magnitude at each of that isochrone's phase-0 points whose initial mass lies inside the phase-0 mass range of the four nearest ages (a_{k-2}, a_{k-1}, a_{k+1}, a_{k+2}), predicted from the other ages by linear interpolation in log age (two neighbours) and by the cubic through the four (Lagrange), after each age's r(m) is interpolated linearly in mass at that mass; the RMS and the maximum of the error in magnitudes, per method; the number of held-out points.
candidates.oracle: scipy.interpolate.interp1d (linear) and scipy.interpolate.BarycentricInterpolator on the four nodes

legs.what: predictions against the oracle: every held-out prediction, both methods, absolute 1e-9 mag
held-out accuracy: the cubic's RMS error is no larger than the linear's, and at most 0.05 mag
legs.bound: both (0.05 mag is a bound chosen here before the run, about the photometric scatter of a rich cluster's main sequence; it is not derived from Gravitas's own isochrone morph)

legs.what: determinism
negative case: a request for an age outside the table's range, or a [Fe/H] the table does not hold, is refused (nothing is extrapolated)
supplies, as N01.e; the example validates through validateObservation; the pack's licence status travels with the example (no-license-stated, attributed) and is stated in the notebook's credit line

candidates.title: A polytrope against the stellar kernel

input.example: made by the spike: tools/compute-gate-polytrope-input.mjs writes js/kernels/stellar/polytrope.js polytropeTable() as a dense grid (axis `n` = TABLE_INDICES; outputs xi1, mass, rhoRatio), the kernel's own values

candidates.computes: The Lane-Emden equation theta'' + 2 theta'/xi + theta^n = 0 from the series start at xi = 1e-6 with scipy solve_ivp (DOP853, rtol = 1e-12, atol = 1e-14) and a terminal event at theta = 0, for every n on the grid's axis: xi1, the dimensionless mass -xi1^2 theta'(xi1), rho_c over the mean density; each compared with the grid.
candidates.oracle: closed forms n = 0 (theta = 1 - xi^2/6: xi1 = sqrt(6), mass = 2 sqrt(6)) and n = 1 (theta = sin(xi)/xi: xi1 = pi, mass = pi), derived here; for the other n an independent solve with scipy solve_ivp Radau (rtol = 1e-11, atol = 1e-13) from the series start at xi = 1e-4

legs.what: analytic cases n = 0 and 1: xi1 and mass relative 1e-9
against the oracle for every other n on the axis: xi1 and mass relative 1e-8
against the stellar kernel's table (the input): xi1, mass and rhoRatio relative 1e-6 for every n
legs.bound: 1e-6 (the kernel integrates with RK4 at a fixed step of 5e-4: its error is far below 1e-6, so a larger difference is a defect in one of the two)

legs.what: determinism
negative cases (all refused): an input whose axis holds n = 5 (infinite radius) or n = 5.5 (infinite mass) or n = -0.5
supplies, as N01.e; the example validates through validateGrid

input.example: made by the spike: a SYNTHETIC snapshot, labelled so in its title and generator, N = 1000 equal masses (1/N each), x and y drawn from independent standard normals with numpy default_rng(268009); axis `body` 0 to 999; outputs x, y, m; G = 1

candidates.computes: Accelerations with Plummer softening eps = 0.05 by direct summation, and by a monopole quadtree (centre of mass per cell, a cell is used when its side over its distance to the body is below theta) for theta = 0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0; for each theta the RMS over bodies of |a_tree - a_direct| / |a_direct|, the maximum, and the number of body-cell and body-body interactions.
candidates.oracle: numpy direct summation written separately; the same snapshot's pinned accelerations

theta = 0 (every cell opened): the tree equals the direct sum, every component relative 1e-10 of the largest
the RMS error is non-decreasing in theta, at most 0.05 at theta = 0.5, and the interactions at theta = 0.5 are at most 0.25 N (N - 1)
legs.bound: all three (0.05 is coarser than the customary monopole error at 0.5; it is a bound set before the run)

verdict.function: A candidate PASSES iff every verdict leg of its own (N**.a to N**.e and the legs lettered for it) is passed, and G2.b and G3.b are passed for it, and every page leg G1.a to G1.c, G2.a, G4.a to G4.c, G5.a, G5.b, G6.a and G7.a is passed. A leg that is not run is not passed. A reported leg decides nothing. A is every candidate passing; B is at least one but not all, and lists them; C is none. Computed by the validator from the committed bounds alone.
verdict.ifNotRun: A verdict leg that needs a request (R1 to R3) and was not run keeps its candidate from PASSing, so with R1 to R3 not granted every candidate is NOT PASSED and the verdict is C by the function, whatever the other legs show. The report states, beside it and labelled as not a verdict, the candidates with no failed leg among the legs that could run (the 'no failure so far' list), so that Carl can see what a grant of R1 to R3 would be deciding.
verdict.reRun: If Carl grants R1 to R3 the same function is re-evaluated on the same file in a follow-up, as the data legs of Prompts 261 and 263 were: no bound moves, and a leg that has already failed stays failed.

amendments.text: Definitions the contract left open, no bound moved. The ages used are k = 2 to K-3 (each has two neighbours on either side, which the cubic needs; 'interior ages k = 1 to K-2' read that way). The held-out masses are those of the held-out isochrone's phase-0 points that lie, inclusive, in the intersection of the phase-0 mass ranges of its four neighbours. At a neighbour, r(m) is the linear interpolation in mass of that age's phase-0 points sorted by mass. The linear method uses the two nearest ages (k-1 and k+1) and the cubic the Lagrange polynomial through the four, both in log age.

A negative case is made by the validator from a committed input by a stated derivation and run through the same harness: N01, N02 and N04 from the Kepler-16 file (N01: body 1's initial position set to body 0's; N02: body 1 placed 1e-6 of the pair separation from body 0 on the line joining them; N04: the first companion's e set to 1.2, and to -0.1); N05 from the TESS file (the first four cadences; and the first 600 with every time set to the first); N06 from the TESS file (the first nine cadences; times reversed; flux set to a constant; a parameter `periods` holding a non-positive trial period); N07 by the parameter `request` (feh and logAge) naming an age 99 and a [Fe/H] the table does not hold; N09 by the parameter `eps` = 0 and by the 4,001-body snapshot; N08 and N10 by the input files tools/compute-gate-inputs.mjs writes. A notebook reads a parameter only if its candidate names one here: `request` (N07), `eps` (N09, default 0.05), `periods` (N06, default the committed 400).

The engine pair, the different-clusters pair and the three synthetic grids are written by tools/compute-gate-inputs.mjs under Node 22.23.4 (the engine pair's sha256 equals the Node 24 run's: checked). N03.b compares the notebook with the oracle on the engine's pair; the oracle also runs the other four grids so that the refusal and recovery legs have an independent decision, and N03.a and N03.d read the notebook's own result against the analytic truth and the refusal rule, not against each other.

amendments.before: the oracle's first run (which stopped at an import error and produced no result)
amendments.text: astropy 6.0.1 cannot import here because PyYAML is not importable (astropy.table imports it for ECSV files, which N06 does not use). The oracle inserts an empty module named `yaml` into sys.modules before importing astropy.timeseries; nothing was installed and nothing was downloaded. The first invocation of the oracle failed at that import before computing anything; no number from it was seen.

amendments.before: the first notebook run (the oracle's output had been seen, no notebook existed)
amendments.text: The oracle refuses the engine's pair under the committed window rule (R^2 below 0.98). Where the oracle's decision is 'refused', N03.b passes iff the notebook also refuses, and the R^2 and the two window ends in the notebook's refusal message (repr of the numbers) equal the oracle's (R^2 to 1e-9). The notebook's refusal message therefore states `R2=`, `i0=` and `i1=` for a refusal on R^2. This is a reading of the leg for the case the oracle decides; it changes no bound and does not make N03.b easier to fail or to pass on a case where the oracle returns a rate. It is stated here because it means that, on the engine's own export, N03 produces no rate (reported: N03.r is then 'refused').

amendments.before: the validator's pinned run (a first attempt was aborted by hand after 12 minutes inside N02's negative case; no leg had been computed or written)
amendments.text: Notebooks run under `python3 -E`, not `python3 -I` as `environment.notebooks` says: -I also drops the user site where numpy and scipy are installed here, so no notebook could import them; the harness is otherwise compute-answers.mjs's. Every notebook run has a wall-clock limit, 900 s, and N02.d's negative case 60 s (its bound is 20 s of CPU; a run that has not refused by 60 s has failed the leg and is killed, and the leg records that). No bound moved.

amendments.about: a defect of the N02 notebook's own code, found by reading its failing legs of the first run (N02.a, N02.b, N02.d)
amendments.text: The prototype's Dormand-Prince stage loop indexed the tableau one row early (stage 2 was computed with the empty row, so every stage after the first used the wrong coefficients): the scheme was not the committed one, and its errors were hundreds of times scipy's at a similar step count. The code is corrected (the stage i uses row i of the tableau, whose constants were checked against scipy's RK45 tableau as a check of the typing, not as a leg). The first run's rows stay in first-run-results.json and in the record as the first stream; the corrected notebook is the candidate N02 judged by the pinned second run. No bound moved and no other notebook's code changed.

amendments.about: a defect of the validator's execution
amendments.text: The validator looked N09's theta rows up by String(theta), but the notebook's keys are Python's repr of a float ('1.0', '0.0'), so theta = 1.0 was read as absent and N09.g's monotone check saw a null. The lookup is corrected to the notebook's keys. No bound moved; the leg's rule is unchanged.

amendments.about: N01.a, N07.b, G4.b, G5.b, G7.a, N02.d (first-run fails that are not defects)
amendments.text: Recorded so that no reader takes the corrections above for a rescue: N01.a (errors against the oracle within 1e-6; measured 1.7e-5 on the smallest error, which differs because the two codes' rounding differences are amplified in a reference whose own error is near 1e-12 against an RK4 error of 7e-9), N07.b (the cubic is not better than the linear), G4.b (no recurring runtime check), G5.b (a built-in course lists five investigations that have a compute step) and G7.a (no room in the route's ceiling) are failures of the legs as committed, and they stay failing and labelled. Each is reported as it stands in the second run.

decisions: DEC1: the ten legs-per-candidate share one shape (accuracy against an independent code, agreement with the Gravitas module the roadmap names, determinism, refusals, supplies), so that a pass or fail is comparable across notebooks and none gets a gentler test.
DEC2: the machine's CPython stands in for the pinned runtime for everything that does not need the browser; every number it produces is labelled CPython and none is offered as a Pyodide result.
DEC3: a leg that needs downloaded code to run is NOT RUN with an exact request; it is not guessed and it is not waived.
DEC4: page legs are shared by all candidates because the roadmap's thresholds 1, 4, 5, 6 and 7 are about the page; a failed page leg removes every candidate (verdict C) and says which leg.
questions: Q1: grant R1 and R2 (run the pinned runtime in Chromium and WebKit) so that G2.b and G3.b are measured? Without them the verdict is C by the function.
Q2: if G4.b fails (no recurring runtime check), is adding one to TOOLCHAIN.md's quarterly pass (129) Carl's to schedule, separate from this gate?
